about: Ask in words' held-out set 3 (metrics; C1724's overfitting guard). Written on 2026-10-26 by an author who had seen no prompt, no earlier held-out case and no recording, and never seen while tuning: no prompt may be changed to fit these questions. Ten questions a network engineer types into History › Query › Ask in words (Metrics) for the network Default (r1-r4, r6-r8 role router; s1-s5 role switch), across memory, interface errors and discards, BGP, switch CPU, restarts, traffic, IP SLA, one question back and one refusal, with a calendar span (yesterday; since Monday, the operator's 2026-10-26 ruling: custom from Monday's midnight) and a relative one (the past week = 7d, the same ruling). Each expectation was decided from the live catalogue BEFORE any model run: read-only probes on the NMAS host, 2026-10-26 20:27 to 20:31 UTC, through modules/history_promq (`catalogue` over 7 days: 854 names; `labels_of` for the devices, roles and jobs each expected metric carries; instant PromQL counts through `_json`). Not yet recorded. `expect` as metrics.json's (cases.misses); `evidence` names the read that backs the case; `flag` says what the evidence alone cannot settle. Three are healthy-nothing cases (s4's input errors, the routers' output discards, router restarts since Monday): the expected query is right and finds nothing.

cases.question: How much free memory does r3 have right now?
cases.evidence: ciscoMemoryPoolFree and cempMemPoolFree are carried by r1-r4, r6-r8 (job cisco_8000v, role router); r3 holds 2 series of each (its pools) at 20:29 UTC. No switch carries either.
cases.flag: 'Right now' is read as the last hour. One line per pool, or the pools summed (r3 is one device, so a group with no label is allowed), are both right; the operations are not judged.

cases.question: Have any of s4's ports been taking input errors over the last day?
cases.evidence: ifInErrors is carried by s4 (8 series, job cisco_vios_l2); increase(ifInErrors{device="s4"}[1d]) > 0 answered 0 series at 20:29 UTC. The IOS-XE telemetry in_errors metric is carried by the routers only, never s4.
cases.flag: Healthy-nothing: the right query finds no errors. A filter or comparison (gt:0) after the rate or increase is allowed and not judged.

cases.question: Total output discards per router over the past week
cases.evidence: ifOutDiscards carries role router on r1-r4, r6-r8 (45 series); increase(ifOutDiscards{role="router"}[7d]) > 0 answered 0 series at 20:29 UTC. The IOS-XE telemetry out_discards (job telemetry_mdt) carries no role label, so a role-router query of it finds nothing.
cases.flag: Healthy-nothing. 'The past week' is 7d (the operator's 2026-10-26 ruling). Naming the seven routers as devices instead of the role is judged a miss though it draws the same lines.

cases.question: Are r4's BGP neighbours established?
cases.evidence: cbgpPeer2State is carried by r3 and r4 only (job bgp, role router); r4 holds 2 peers, both value 6 (established) at 20:29 UTC.
cases.flag: No time is said: the builder's default 24h or the last hour are both accepted. An eq:6 comparison is allowed and not judged.

cases.question: Show me the top 5 switches by CPU load over the last hour
cases.evidence: cpuAvgBusy1, cpuAvgBusy5 and cpuBusyPer are carried by s1-s5 only (job cisco_vios_l2, role switch), 5 series each at 20:29 UTC; cpmCPUTotal1minRev and cpmCPUTotal5minRev are routers only.
cases.flag: The network has exactly five switches, so top 5 shows all of them. Naming s1-s5 as devices instead of the role is judged a miss.

cases.question: Has any router rebooted since Monday?
cases.evidence: sysUpTime carries role router on r1-r4, r6-r8 (7 series); resets(sysUpTime{role="router"}[73798s]) > 0 (since 26 Oct 00:00 UTC) answered 0 series at 20:29 UTC.
cases.flag: Healthy-nothing. 'Since Monday' is From Monday's midnight to now (the operator's 2026-10-26 ruling); written on Monday 26 Oct, when this week and today begin at the same midnight. changes is not accepted: uptime changes at every scrape. resets is prompt v8's operation (schema v3); an earlier schema cannot answer it.

cases.question: What was r1's inbound traffic in bits per second yesterday?
cases.evidence: r1 carries ifHCInOctets on 6 interfaces at 26 Oct 00:00 UTC, 3 of them moving over 25 Oct (increase over 1d > 0); ifInOctets and the IOS-XE telemetry in_octets are carried by r1 too.
cases.flag: Per-interface lines or their sum for r1 are both right; a sum is not judged.

cases.question: Plot the IP SLA round-trip time from r2 for the last 30 days
cases.evidence: rttMonLatestRttOperCompletionTime is carried by r1-r4, s2 and s3 (job cisco_ipsla); r2 holds 2 probes at 20:29 UTC, present 7 days back, absent 30 days back (retention 90d).
cases.flag: r2's probes began inside the 30 days, so the graph starts partway; the expectation is still the 30-day range asked.

cases.question: Is that interface still flapping?
cases.evidence: ifOperStatus is carried by all twelve devices (89 interfaces carry ifHCInOctets at 20:3x UTC); the question names no device and no interface, and 'that' refers to nothing on a fresh ask.
cases.flag: Mercury's own guidance counts as a question back (cases.misses). An answer of changes(ifOperStatus) across the whole network is a guess at which interface is meant. (A first draft, 'Is the uplink maxed out?', was dropped before any run: three interfaces on r6, r7 and r8 carry 'uplink' in ifAlias, so an answer filtering on it is defensible.)

cases.question: What's the chassis temperature on s3?
cases.evidence: No name among the catalogue's 854 matches temp, therm, sensor, fan, env or power; no series with such a name exists for s3 or any device at 20:29 UTC.
cases.flag: Mercury's guide (no metric matches) is accepted beside the model's refusal.
